text: maya: quick Q — for the new 'Create Endpoint' form: do we prefer an asterisk (*) for required fields or the explicit 'Required' label? also thinking about how errors should show for multi-field rows (eg. CPU/GPU selection). Any accessibility concerns? :eyes: sam: my gut is explicit 'Required' for clarity, but worried about visual noise if there are a lot of fields. maybe hide on low-density forms? jordan: +1 for explicit label. asterisk is ambiguous for some folks, and screen readers don't always announce it by default. if we use asterisk we should also include aria-label or visually-hidden text. maya: good point — we need something that both sighted users and screen-readers get. Alex, can you weigh in on SR/aria best practice? :accessibility: alex: screen readers: prefer semantic attributes. set aria-required="true" and connect labels properly. visually-hidden "Required" text is fine. example snippet we use elsewhere: `````` also, don't rely on color alone for required/error states (contrast + icon + text). kevin: re: multi-field rows — if fields are interdependent (like CPU/GPU) showing one inline error per field can be noisy. proposal: inline micro-errors under each field, but show a compact grouped summary at top on submit with anchors to the fields. keeps inline guidance and gives overview. sam: that matches product goals — quick inline fixes plus top-level summary for keyboard users. on submit, the summary should be first thing a screen reader lands on. jordan: UX nit — for inline errors on blur vs on submit: recommend validate-on-blur for better feedback, but only show red error after user interaction; don't show errors for untouched fields on page load. maya: agree. also want to discuss destructive confirmations (delete endpoint / purge logs). do we prefer modal with typed confirmation (type resource name) or a checkbox + secondary CTA? kevin: typed confirmation is safest for irreversible actions, but increases friction. for idempotent or semi-reversible stuff a checkbox + explicit CTA is fine. maybe escalate: start with checkbox for less-dangerous, force typed input for full-delete actions. alex: accessibility for typed confirmations — ensure the input has clear label, error states accessible, and if we require exact match be careful about case-sensitivity (prefer case-insensitive match to avoid accessibility friction). maya: good call. also should we surface the consequences inline near the control (small summary) so keyboard users can read before opening modal? sam: yes, put a short sentence under the action button: "This will permanently delete model variants and metrics." and link to docs. jordan: small UI idea — for grouped fields, use background grouping + soft border and put a group-level required marker (with sr-only text) so we don't repeat label text at field level. helps scanning. alex: accessibility checklist reminder: focus management when errors shown (move focus to first error), announce summary role=alert region for screen readers, ensure focus trapped in modals and restore after close. maya: thanks all. next steps: @jordan create a small prototype (Figma + HTML) with explicit 'Required' label + inline blur validation + top summary on submit. include one destructive action example with typed confirm and one with checkbox. i'll review tomorrow. :thumbsup: jordan: on it, will iterate and ping for review. design-bot: Reminder — design critique scheduled 2026-04-01 10:00 PT. Agenda: forms validation patterns, destructive confirmations, accessibility nits.
